name: ASAP 2.0
summary: About 24,000 source-based persuasive essays by students in grades 6, 8, 9 and 10, with human scores, the rubric and the source texts.

license.note: CC BY 4.0 since 2026-01-20; earlier copies say CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. About half its essays are also in PERSUADE 2.0.

cite: Crossley, S. A., Baffour, P., Burleigh, L., & King, J. (2025). A large-scale corpus for assessing source-based writing quality: ASAP 2.0. Assessing Writing, 65, 100954. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asw.2025.100954

fits.how: Its scored essays and rubric are a set to check a model's reading of writing against trained raters.

connect.note: Does a model reading an essay land on the same side of "adequate mastery" as trained raters? The same number of essays from each score, with their rubric. A pass or fail on one line, so it isn't the score agreement papers report. Writers' demographics are dropped at download. It says nothing about whether feedback helps. These are real students' essays, masked by their makers: running this sends them to the model you name, so use one whose terms you accept.
